base_member_text: [L74-L92, L767-L771] (MED/conditional-allocation) Old-state arrays are allocated only if second-order or nonhydrostatic mode is active on the first call; because later allocation is gated by vsu, enabling either mode on a reused instance would access unallocated uu_old, vv_old, and zs_old.

[L74-L122] (LOW/lifecycle-contract) All saved work arrays and bed-roughness initialization are keyed to a one-time allocation test with no grid-shape or parameter-change check, making reinitialization semantics implicit.
audit_member_text: [L74-L122,L635-L656,L645-L652,L767-L771] (MED/state/configuration lifecycle) Old-state arrays are allocated only if second-order or nonhydrostatic mode is active on the first call, so enabling either mode later accesses unallocated storage; all saved work arrays also retain the first grid shape.

adversarial.rationale: This is a reuse or externally changed-configuration defect, rather than a failure during an ordinary fixed-configuration run. The standard parameter setup fixes the modes before the first call, but a second lifecycle with changed dimensions or later enabling a mode can bypass the required saved allocations.
adversarial.verified_by: llm:codex independent skeptic + caller verbatim neutralizer re-check

base_member_text: [L618-L627] (HIGH/boundary-condition-selection) The left global boundary calls flow_lat_bc with par%right while the right global boundary passes par%left, apparently swapping the configured lateral boundary types.
audit_member_text: [L621-L627] (MED/boundary-condition mapping) The physical left boundary passes par%right to flow_lat_bc while the physical right boundary passes par%left, an unexplained reversal of boundary configuration.

adversarial.rationale: The claim confuses MPI array-layout names with physical boundary names. The parameter declarations explicitly define left at ny+1 and right at zero, exactly matching the calls in flow_timestep.

base_member_text: [L512-L525] (MED/mask-typo) The Smagorinsky cross-stress dudy term for v uses wetv(i-1,j) as its fourth mask while the other three factors and the differentiated field are u-point quantities, suggesting one wetv should be wetu.
audit_member_text: [L512-L526] (HIGH/wrong wet-mask component) The Smagorinsky cross-stress mask for V momentum multiplies three wetu values but uses wetv(i-1,j) for the fourth point, inconsistent with the U-velocity stencil.

adversarial.rationale: The viscosity stencil combines three U wet flags with a V wet flag at the fourth location. Wetcells derives those flags independently from different face depths, so neither their declarations nor the stencil context makes them interchangeable.
adversarial.verified_by: llm:codex independent skeptic + caller verbatim neutralizer re-check

base_member_text: [L866-L876, L956-L985] (HIGH/unassigned-boundary-state) s%ue at i=nx+1 and, in 2-D, s%ve at j=ny+1 are not assigned, yet the vertical-profile loop consumes both arrays over 1:nx+1 and 1:ny+1, so wet edge cells can use initialization-era or stale velocities.

[L805-L853, L877-L934] (MED/partial-array-update) Several staggered interpolants (vu/vsu/usu and uv/vsv/usv) update only interior slices and explicitly leave some process-edge rows or columns unresolved; multiplying by a wet mask does not refresh previously wet, still-wet omitted entries.
audit_member_text: [L776-L794,L805-L853,L866-L936] (HIGH/stale interpolation boundaries) Multiple cell/face interpolants (vu, vsu, usu, uv, vsv, usv, ue, and ve) leave MPI-internal halo rows/columns or nx+1/ny+1 edges unset, as the inline comments acknowledge, yet whole-array velocity magnitudes consume them.

adversarial.rationale: The saved interpolants are initially zeroed, so the issue is stale or incorrect boundary/halo values rather than wholly uninitialized storage on the first call. Several later assignments still leave edges unchanged before whole-array magnitudes are formed, and no intervening interpolation exchange fills them.

base_member_text: [L365-L369, L469-L530, L593-L615] (MED/stale-disabled-term) When viscosity is disabled the code zeros nuh and viscu but not viscv, so a reused state that changes viscosity mode can retain the previous y-momentum viscous acceleration.
audit_member_text: [L365-L369,L471-L478,L593-L617] (MED/stale disabled-viscosity component) The viscosity-off branch clears nuh and viscu but not viscv, so a runtime transition from enabled to disabled viscosity leaves the prior V-viscous acceleration active.

adversarial.rationale: The residual V acceleration requires viscosity to have been enabled previously and then disabled through configuration reuse or an external parameter change. The normal fixed-parameter run does not make that transition, but the off branch really clears only nuh and viscu while the V update can still consume viscv.
adversarial.verified_by: llm:codex independent skeptic + caller verbatim neutralizer re-check

base_member_text: [L956-L972] (LOW/roughness-location-contract) The cell-centered vertical-profile call derives ks directly from u-point cfu(i,j) without documenting interpolation or guarding the positive-friction prerequisite.
audit_member_text: [L956-L972] (MED/singular profile inputs) The vertical-profile call derives ks using sqrt(g/cfu) without ensuring positive cfu and passes potentially zero sigm/k values into a routine that divides by both.

adversarial.rationale: The VSM caller checks wetz and nz but does not require positive cfu before sqrt(g/cfu) or ensure the resulting ks is nonzero. Coefficient inputs can supply zero, and positive depth does not prevent either the caller division or the later roughness singularities.
adversarial.verified_by: llm:codex independent skeptic + caller verbatim neutralizer re-check

base_member_text: [L660-L719] (MED/positivity-preservation) hu and hv are clamped nonnegative before flow_secondorder_huhv, but the second-order correction can subtract from them and there is no subsequent positivity clamp before forming qx and qy.

[L721-L722] (LOW/staggering-contract) qmag combines qx and qy elementwise even though they are stored at different staggered locations, so the stated output magnitude lacks an explicit interpolation convention.

audit_member_text: [L1046-L1063] (MED/boundary stencil contract) The 2-D Smagorinsky stencil reads i±1 and j±1 at generic computational bounds under an explicit MPI-warning comment, without local bounds/halo validation.
